findings.finding: The original bound ligand has 25 heavy atoms and covariance eigenvalues 0.111, 5.696 and 9.303 A2, supporting a nearly planar, anisotropic pose reference. This is static geometry, not evidence that this shape improves generated-ligand pIC50.

LEU45, ILE174 and VAL66 each neighbor 9-10 ligand atoms within 4.5 A, suggesting distributed pocket occupancy as a design hypothesis. PHE113 has the largest listed proxy sum (18.712) despite only six neighboring ligand atoms; atom counts and distance weighting affect this untyped proxy.

Reported nearest-protein distance quantiles span 2.858-4.005 A with median 3.682 A. They describe the occupied reference pose near the formula's 3.6 A contact shell, but do not establish an optimal contact distance or attractive interaction.

The receptor crop contains 308 heavy atoms within a reported 12 A radius. Its protein-neighbor distance quantiles describe receptor geometry; they cannot establish ligand clash frequency or ligand-receptor repulsion strength.

The supplied geometry has no affinity labels. No score, trajectory, selection comparison or teacher pointcloud is supplied, so historical enrichment, survival and temporal trends are unavailable in this request.

directions: Compare registered structure and pocket controls under the supplied seed, 100 steps and [0, 0.5] window, evaluating final predicted pIC50 and secondary strain; the reference pose alone cannot select a winner.

For structure and pocket, compare contact_weight 0, 0.25 and 0.5 with other settings fixed, using ligand-receptor distances and occupancy across the listed regions to test the geometric contact hypothesis.

For structure, compare ligand_anchor_weight 0.5, 1 and 2 while holding contact and repulsion fixed; assess pose retention alongside pIC50, strain and graph transitions to test the value of the planar reference.

Evaluate repulsion_weight 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 only in structure or pocket, against observed generated ligand-receptor distances below 2 A. Treat native_rms_ratio and time_ramp_power changes as prospective experiments, not historically supported trends.
limitations: Only original receptor and bound-ligand summaries are observed; formula registry descriptions do not expose selected historical coordinates or outcomes.
The listed regions are a subset of 53, and summaries omit full atom coordinates, atom types and interaction labels. They cannot support an affinity or physical-energy interpretation.
The compression note mentions selected q-values, but no comparison table or q-value is supplied; no statistical association or enrichment estimate can be reported.
All proposed updates are unvalidated hypotheses within registered parameter support. A single seed and static reference cannot establish robustness, strain improvement or the best formula.
